old: as in Keynes’s 1944 proposal for a clearing union
new: as in Keynes’s wartime proposal for an International Clearing Union (published in 1943)
why: Keynes’s clearing-union plan was drafted in 1941–42 and published as a British White Paper in April 1943; at Bretton Woods in 1944 the negotiations proceeded largely on the US (White) plan.

old: US crude oil production peaked in 1970, leaving
new: US crude oil production reached a peak in 1970 that was not exceeded until 2018, leaving
why: EIA data show annual US crude output (about 9.6 million barrels a day in 1970) was surpassed in 2018, so an unqualified ‘peaked’ is now misleading as a stated fact.

old: impose an embargo on the United States after the Yom Kippur War
new: impose an embargo on the United States during the Yom Kippur War
why: The OAPEC cuts (17 October) and the Saudi-led embargo on the US (from about 20 October 1973) came while the war was still being fought; the ceasefire followed on 25 October.

old: taking large stakes in the Royal Bank of Scotland and Lloyds Banking Group
new: taking large stakes in the Royal Bank of Scotland and in Lloyds TSB and HBOS (merged as Lloyds Banking Group in January 2009)
why: In October 2008 the recapitalisation covered Lloyds TSB and HBOS separately; Lloyds Banking Group was formed only when their merger completed in January 2009.

old: Greek banks close and capital controls begin; voters reject
new: After banks closed and capital controls began on 29 June, Greek voters reject
why: Greek banks shut and capital controls took effect on 29 June 2015, before the 5 July referendum, not in July as the entry’s date implies.

old: Some theorists, including Guido Lorenzoni and Iván Werning with co-authors, showed in 2020
new: Veronica Guerrieri, Guido Lorenzoni, Ludwig Straub and Iván Werning argued in 2020
why: The ‘Keynesian supply shock’ paper (NBER Working Paper 26918, 2020) is by Guerrieri, Lorenzoni, Straub and Werning, with Guerrieri as first author; naming only two of the four misattributes it.

old: Provided emergency credit in January 1991 and a stand-by arrangement in October 1991, with conditions
new: The IMF provided emergency credit in January 1991 and a stand-by arrangement in October 1991, and the World Bank followed with adjustment lending, with conditions
why: The January 1991 emergency drawings (first credit tranche and CCFF) and the October 1991 stand-by were IMF lending; the World Bank’s structural adjustment loan came later in 1991, as timeline.9 itself says.
